cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: compaction is much better now so for certain things you may not need to explicitly clear
cards.claim: CHANGE OF POSITION: better compaction means you often no longer need to clear or externalize context for model focus, though it is still useful for human collaboration and handoff between agents or machines.
cards.landing: Phase routine's one-phase-per-new-session defence; handoff files stay justified for agent handoff

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I usually my autocompact to 400k and tend to do a manual compact between 200-400k
cards.claim: On 1M-context frontier models he sets auto-compact at 400k and compacts manually between 200k and 400k depending on model and harness, clearing less than before.
cards.landing: Auto-compaction window threshold (harness considers only past 500k)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: "dumb zone" a little more flexible for 1m frontier models.
cards.claim: The dumb zone is more flexible on 1M-context frontier models than earlier fixed-fraction guidance suggested.
cards.evidence_detail: No numbers beyond the 200-400k working range.
cards.landing: Context budget rule in the phase routine

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: i don't think there's any good reason to go beyond 3-levels of subagent nesting today
cards.claim: A top-level orchestrator launching sub-agents that launch their own sub-agents (three tiers) lets the orchestrator steer two levels instead of the human, and he sees no reason to nest deeper for most tasks.
cards.landing: Workflow-tool orchestration depth (main session, readers, refuters)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: your intuition as to whether model is on track or getting dumb is always the best source!
cards.claim: These thresholds are training wheels; the operator's own judgement of whether the model is on track outranks any fixed number.
cards.landing: Closing-message / owner-view check on drift

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: just go from source every time
cards.claim: A doc or per-directory compacted summary is only justified if it raises speed without lowering quality, and absent codebase-specific evals watched closely the simpler answer is to accept a speed hit and read source each time.
cards.evidence_detail: Opinion; he declines to endorse a cited $32m paper.
cards.landing: Knowledge-store pilot design and P1 cold-resume trial (store vs source baseline)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: codebases for humans" vs "codebases for agents
cards.claim: He objects to the framing of codebases for humans versus codebases for agents, and notes docs remain a primary source when the code is closed and users' agents must integrate it.
cards.landing: Docs/CODE-MAP role versus reading source

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Subagent overuse and abuse has been a problem since mid 2025.
cards.claim: Sub-agents are high leverage in the right place but the hype culture pushes more parallelism instead of careful context management.
cards.evidence_detail: Reacts to an Anthropic article recommending folding unneeded sub-agents into the main loop.
cards.landing: Sizing the 11 new agent definitions; justify each against a skill

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Conflating context management with instruction modules (these are quite orthogonal concerns)
cards.claim: Sub-agents manage context while skills are the instruction modules; before skills sub-agents were the only way to hold different system prompts, now skills are the better method and can be invoked from parent or sub-agent.
cards.landing: Choosing skill package versus agent definition for each fixflow-* item

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: 90% of subagent usage is ppl playing house
cards.claim: Sub-agents are good for code research and sequential sub-context implementation, but about 90% of sub-agent usage is role-play.
cards.landing: Keep the Haiku file locator; scrutinize role-named agents

cards.source_title: @dexhorthy post 2026-10-25 on stacking skills in one session
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: my intuition says 5 steps in a process is fine.
cards.claim: Running a five-step process with a skill per step in a single session is fine, since each skill takes some attention from earlier ones.
cards.landing: Phase routine steps as skills in one session

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you want fresh context, subagents, or to synthetically precombine many skill contents
cards.claim: When skills must stack (skill 2's rules still binding during skill 6) or ~200 skills must be active, use fresh context, sub-agents, or precombine into one user message, at the cost of recency bias; agent memory as skills is probably an anti-pattern.
cards.evidence_detail: Reasoned heuristic; 200 is an illustrative count.
cards.landing: Skill-package count and loading policy; knowledge store as skills

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Adherence can decay over a long session.
cards.claim: Behavioural rules in skills decay over a long session, so repeat important rules in every step of a process or enforce them with something deterministic like hooks; instruction-heavy skills should be strung out, information-heavy ones can be combined.
cards.landing: Hooks the harness review skipped; phase-routine rule repetition

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: PLEASE stop putting stuff that’s in the weights in your skills.
cards.claim: Content already in the model weights should not go in skills, as it wastes time and locks in a specific, possibly suboptimal behaviour.
cards.landing: Audit CLAUDE.md and the 13 skill packages for generic content

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: If the skill contents look correct, delete the skill. It’s in the weights.
cards.claim: To test whether a skill is redundant, ask the model to write that skill with light steering, read it, and delete your skill if the generated one looks correct.
cards.landing: Pruning check for CLAUDE.md trim and skill packages

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: do less in parallel, elevate getting things #1/2 done over maximizing utilization
cards.claim: Slow down, prioritize, and run less in parallel, even at the cost of idle time for the human.
cards.evidence_detail: Opinion; echoes his earlier limit-WIP post (30 years since XP/Lean).
cards.landing: One phase per new session; owner view

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: a good software factory starts with measurement, then self improvement against those metrics
cards.claim: A software factory should start with measurement then self-improve against those metrics, and turn successful agent runs into evals for testing future models and harnesses.
cards.evidence_detail: Dex's bullet summary of a video with Zach Lloyd and Vaibhav; video not read.
cards.landing: Measurement pipeline the review skipped; evidence folders as eval seeds

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: why counting lines of code is bad metric, and why counting PRs might be good enough
cards.claim: Lines of code is a bad productivity metric, and counting PRs (with DORA) may be good enough.
cards.landing: One-page owner view metrics

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: term software factory is being semantically diffused
cards.claim: The term software factory is diffusing through hype, but the pre-AI NATO/DoD concept of automating more things remains a useful mental model.
cards.landing: Vocabulary in program docs

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the best products in software factory space are building blocks, not drop in solutions
cards.claim: The key parts of a factory (stack, linters, tests, previews) are too heterogeneous to generalize in a product, so building blocks beat drop-in solutions and vendors disappoint.
cards.landing: Per-repo verifiers and a reusable workflow library rather than a bought factory

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: this technique had already been demonstrated and so was likely present in the weights
cards.claim: Apparently novel model behaviour (agents using processor cache to pass secrets) is likely recombination of techniques already in the weights, not invention.
cards.evidence_detail: Commentary on OpenAI sandbox escape anecdote.
cards.landing: Sandbox/permission assumptions for agent runs

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the worst parts of most people’s days are reading verbose, AI-written slack messages
cards.claim: CHANGE OF POSITION: his 2024 claim that models excel at relaying context now looks naive; models do deep technical work and the worst part of people's days is unreviewed verbose AI-written messages and docs.
cards.landing: Output caps and brevity rules for agent-written PR bodies, closing messages and owner view

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: this guy gets it
cards.claim: Endorses a third party's view that the bottleneck is shifting from reviewing intent to human decision-making across many contexts, needing per-decision command centers.
cards.evidence_detail: Endorsement of Plannotator-style author's post; author is other.
cards.landing: One-page owner view as decision surface

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: what we actually need is more skill packs
cards.claim: He argues more skill packs, not more tooling, are what is needed (image only, no further text).
cards.evidence_detail: One line plus a photo not seen; possibly ironic.
cards.landing: 13 skill packages in PR #185

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Why is slop worth fighting?
cards.claim: He is preparing material with swyx/AI Engineer on defining slop, why it happens and how to prevent it, soliciting input (a pointer to upcoming content, no answers yet).
cards.landing: Watch for the resulting slop-prevention content

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Twelve Factor Factories: Design Patterns for Agentic Engineering
cards.claim: He announced a talk combining 12-factor agents with software factories as design patterns for agentic engineering (about 2026-11-12), plus recalling RPI as context engineering and semantic diffusion.
cards.evidence_detail: Talk announcement; content not yet available.
cards.landing: Source to read once published

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Great engineers want flexible, composable tools, not monolithic, opinionated black-boxes.
cards.claim: Their stated shared principle is composable tools over monolithic black-boxes, and large multi-repo teams are poorly served by off-the-shelf coding agents and harnesses.
cards.landing: Supports a self-built composable harness

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: multiplayer tasks/workstreams, in-app collaboration on docs and plans, and live session diff streaming
cards.claim: Next in Factory: multiplayer tasks/workstreams, collaboration on docs and plans, live diff streaming, and open-sourcing HumanLayer, so HumanLayer-based tooling will migrate to Factory.
cards.landing: Dependence risk if the harness borrows HumanLayer RPI skills/repo

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: its time.
cards.claim: HumanLayer core was open-sourced (same code as the cloud), with a third-party recap noting it needs WorkOS/Slack/Linear keys to start; article body not present in my bundle.
cards.evidence_detail: Only a Chinese-language third-party recap read.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

The 2026-10-23 Open sourcing HumanLayer article body was not in this bundle.
